reviews.title: Helps me not get distracted
reviews.text:
I often found myself opening an app for a specific purpose only to get distracted seeing the little number of notifications on the top right of app icons. Sometimes, I wouldn’t even accomplish what I opened my phone to do. 

Simplifying my home screen has made it so I have access to my most important apps. If I need to use a specific app, I’ll search for it directly; eliminating the potential distractions altogether. Definitely recommend.

reviews.title: Tricky to setup but worth it
reviews.text: Really interesting app. Gives a cool, minimalist interface to your phone. Honestly, I like that it makes my iPhone more unique. Everyone’s phone is the same now and it’s so boring. Yes, it’s designed to reduce your distractions and dependency on your phone. And, that all works really well. But it also just makes your phone cooler. It is tricky to setup. Follow the steps and videos very closely. You’ll figure it out. Also, email them for tech support. They respond promptly. They know it is tricky to configure and are super helpful.

reviews.title: Great until it wasn’t
reviews.text: This app was GREAT and did it exactly what it needed to do until at some point it just started showing me ads; every time I would click on one of my “Dumb Phone apps” it would open up an ad on the actual Dumb Phone app rather than opening up the iMessage app or Camera app. I would try clicking it two or three more times and the ad would just keep showing up. So I am now deleting this app lol

reviews.title: Great app
reviews.text: Love the app. It keeps all the functionality of a smartphone while both reduces the addictive hijacking that comes from just opening your phone and adding just right amount of friction to accessing the full power of the phone. It’s been a great experience. 10/10 recommendation.

reviews.title: Paywall
reviews.text: Force you behind a paywall after I guess a week? I mean I would rather them have just said it more clearly up front before making all these changes. Don’t recommend unless you plan on paying.

reviews.title: Great choice to reduce screen time
reviews.text: I’ve only had this app for about a week and I’ve already had a decrease in my screen time by 34% compared to the previous week. I like how there’s a detox option. When you want to turn off the detox option, there’s a few steps to where you might decide you actually don’t want to turn it back on. In the past I’ve deleted social media apps, but I like to still have the option to stay up to date on local events. Def recommend

reviews.title: Fantastic app
reviews.text: Out of all the minimalist phone apps available (I tried them all), this one stands out. I love that I can integrate widgets directly into my wallpaper to preserve my personal style. Great work 👏

reviews.title: In theory…
reviews.text: I paid the $10 for the year because I felt the opportunity to remove distractions was worth a try. Unfortunately, iPhone doesn’t allow you to hide the App Library from your screen, so getting to an app you don’t want in your face all day is still just one swipe away. In theory, the list (rather than app icons) would limit distractions, but one swipe, and OPE there’s all my apps.

reviews.title: Good app 👍
reviews.text: Pretty good app! If you follow the instructions, it’ll work exactly as described.

reviews.title: Great app
reviews.text: Love this app! I’ve been using the paid version for almost 2 years now, and it’s well worth the small fee. Seeing the home screens on other people’s phones now stresses me out because I’ve gotten so used to my minimal screen. I go back and forth between using the app limits depending on how I’m feeling. It’s definitely improved my phone experience overall, and I have recommended to many a friend!

reviews.title: Don’t pay for the Subscription
reviews.text: Truly a waste of time, do not buy this paid app that is just a widget. Set up your focus time on your phone for free. I made the mistake of paying $25 and I highly doubt they will give a refund. They give you a free trial, but I thought the app was just free. I paid $25 looking for a more intuitive, seamless “dumb phone” but it was the same, widget, buggy launcher that I had. Don’t make my mistake, and give me a refund.

reviews.title: Worth It
reviews.text: I tried other free alternative launchers, but their configuration was more vague and complicated than dp, and their apps were less feature-rich overall. I especially appreciate the breadth of preconfigured shortcuts, custom launchers and Focus Filters, and detailed setup instructions included in dp. As someone with ADHD, the less friction there is with initial setup, the more likely I am to actually stick to a plan. I    purchased a lifetime license because I think dp is worth it for helping me reach my goals for using my phone less.

reviews.title: Dumb phone, not the dumbest app
reviews.text: I got dumb phone as a free alternative to the blank app. I already had some measures in order to stop consuming as much short form content on my phone. Actually, by the time I downloaded dumb phone I did not need apps like TikTok or instagram anymore. This app was more of a means to make my phone less convenient in order to further lessen screen time. Overall, it wasn’t the most effective as it is very easy to overcome its limits if you get incredibly desperate, but its overall not bad, especially for someone who’s already less dependent on the dopamine of short form content. Overall, however, something that I’d recommend much more is something like PushBlock. It’s another free app with a similar but also different usage and structure. On this app, you get to choose different apps that you can restrict almost completely, and the only way to overcome this is, you guessed it, doing pushups. As a lazy bum who’s also trying to get better at body weight exercises like pushups, this has been a very good way of both discouraging myself and getting to do more exercise at more times throughout the day.

reviews.title: Life is Better Minimal
reviews.text: I’ve been using Dumb Phone for 6-8 months. DP has significantly reduced my screen time. Due to the simplistic black and white setup, my phone still looks good, but I’m no longer manipulated by all of the colorful apps that need to be “checked on” constantly. I’m also on social media apps far less. The developer/ owner is very responsive if you have a request. Best money spent. This is a no brainer if you want more actual productivity.

reviews.title: Just a widget

This is nothing more than a widget that gives you plain text shortcuts to apps you choose. 

You still get notifications of all the other apps on your phone. 

The basic UI of the iPhone is not hidden. Everything still works. This is not as described.

reviews.title: Scam- get an actual Dumb phone

reviews.title: This app cuts down on my phone’s distractibility
reviews.text:
This app makes my Home Screen so much less distracting and my interactions with my phone much more intentional. Instead of opening my phone and getting sidetracked by notifications, banners, or whatever app catches my eye, I actually go to the app I intended to use in the first place.

It’s such a simple change, but it’s made a noticeable difference in how I use my phone. The developer is also incredibly responsive, which is a huge plus!

reviews.title: Can’t live without
reviews.text: I’m a content creator, but I’m also a homeschool mom so I wake up in the morning before my kids, make my videos, post them on social media and then lock up my phone before they wake up. Then in the evenings once they’re asleep, I unlock it and respond to comments! This makes it the best of both worlds! And as a mom, it can be really overstimulating. It’s so easy to just pull up your phone and press Facebook using this app makes it harder to check out and makes it so much easier to be intentional with the little kids who are right in front of me!

reviews.title: Great App, Great Support
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app for almost a year and I love it. It has made my phone easy to manage and reduces decision fatigue (no more staring at my phone apps trying to remember which one is the one I’m looking for).  It takes a very short time to set up the display for your phone and anytime you reach out to the “help desk”, you get a personal response within a day. I’ve never felt like an app actually cares about its users but this one does. It’s great.

reviews.title: $10 a year for the app picker to never work
reviews.text: It’s insane to me that this issue hasn’t been fixed yet. Every time I go to revise which apps I want to restrict, it is insanely buggy. I have to move incredibly slowly so that nothing shuts down. Insane.

reviews.title: The only thing that has clicked
reviews.text: This is it, this is the one. I’m the type of guy that tries every single thing people make. Open source, closed, free, paid. This tool has had a huge impact on my well being and productivity via the NFC lock and amazing UI. It’s just so easy to use and fun to lock my phone down and check back into the real world. Well worth the price.

reviews.title: Highly Recommend
reviews.text: I really like Dumb Phone. It has helped me make my phone feel much less distracting while still letting me keep all the apps I actually need. The minimalist layout makes me less tempted to mindlessly open apps or scroll, and I find myself using my phone more intentionally now. It’s simple, clean, and does exactly what I wanted it to do. Definitely recommend it if you want to cut down on screen time without completely switching to an actual dumb phone.

They provide no free trial to test the widget, makes you sign up for a subscription to even use it (no free with ads type deal), and apparently offer no way to get a refund once you realize you got hooked in and scammed. Highly would not recommend paying for a screenshot of black for a background and a couple of mediocre at best widgets.

reviews.title: Light Phone for iPhone
reviews.text: I was seriously considering getting a Light Phone, but after talking to some of my friends who have it I realized I would probably still need an iPhone in addition to the Light Phone. Dumb Phone essentially turns your iPhone into a Light Phone, and it’s completely changed my relationship with my phone. Now it feels like a tool that enhances my life instead of a source of entertainment that distracts from it.

reviews.title: Efficiency & Simplicity
reviews.text:
I’ve been partaking and dabbling w/ Dumb Phone for just over a year now. It’s simple, sleek, clean and helped cut my screen time down by 2/3s.

There’s still a level of self discipline required to reclaim lost time scrolling and wasting our lives away on these dopamine devices, but Dumb Phone is the gateway to making that happen.

reviews.title: Top Tier Alternative Home Screen
reviews.text:
An excellent app. The developer is incredibly responsive and has created an app that sets out to make a less overwhelming Home Screen. I believe he has done it. It’s a great app that mimics a “light phone” type setup for those looking to be more intentional in their phone use. 
Plus honestly I think it just looks nice. It’s also incredibly easy to set up as well thanks to all of the well thought out knowledgebase articles and walk-throughs during setup.

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: It doesn’t have a simple list of the installed apps and web page shortcuts on the phone. Instead it has a massive list of pre approved apps so I have to do a search every time I update my lists. This limitation directly counters the purpose of the app. Other than this, it’s fairly useful but I won’t give it a good rating until this major limitation is fixed. At the very least give me a list at the top of just my apps.

reviews.title: Intentional Phone Use Heaven
reviews.text: This is my second year using Dumb Phone. Last year, when I started using it, I had downloaded it looking for something to help me be more intentional with my day because I was (and still am) a stay at home mom. I didn’t want scrolling to get in the way of the connection I wanted to make with my young child, so downloading this app has been incredibly helpful. My favorite parts about this app are how you can list the apps on your phone screen to make it boring and low-key, so the doping addiction doesn’t get in the way of your day and it keeps you from being awake all night so you can actually take care of your sleep hygiene. I also thoroughly enjoy that I can’t bypass certain app timers just to get back to an app to scroll.

reviews.title: Worth a try
reviews.text: I’ve been wanting to keep my iPhone while minimizing screen time and it having less of a grab on me. So far it’s worked and the set up steps are easy to do and make your phone more of a tool then a stimulating pocket computer. 1 week free trail is a no brainer try it
